selection.rationale: Composition experiment: the accepted region bundle trial-0b17ae710c-param-a2600a0f (decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM.forward, call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, route eager_flat_decode_ws) must stay active, so the second candidate edits complementary group sites that provably execute inside it: every selected decode-phase functional site has site_parent 323bcbe006b343648b346af9 in current discovery, so functional dispatch composes with the region implementation rather than replacing it, and the bundle's required module call keeps running every decode step. Cost evidence from the current discovery run (562.18 ms device time; decode module 430.30 ms; clean wall ~731 ms at the accepted 349.96 tok/s) shows the accepted version is now overhead-bound: ~170 ms of wall-CPU/launch gap over ~2,000 kernel launches per decode step. The six decode aten::linear groups (319.7 ms, cutlass_80_wmma 32-thread-block kernels) are deliberately NOT selected: historical trial-9cc583939d on this same model proved that changing GEMM accumulation order (gate/up packing, N 9728->19456) puts 27.2% of logits out of tolerance (max abs 1.96875, max rel 15424) even with identical greedy tokens, and the same amplification applies to q/k/v/o/gate/up/down at decode; sdpa (20.7 ms) and the mean/pow reduction kernels are excluded for the same reduction-order reason, and prefill GEMMs already run at ~156 TFLOPS. The quality bar that the accepted bundle met with max_abs_error 0.0 leaves exactly one safe mechanism class: byte-identical elimination of eager op overhead. The selected 26 groups are the complete set of decode elementwise sites of three per-layer chains issued by the active bundle: (a) RMSNorm tails after the untouched mean+eps kernels - rsqrt, x32*rstd mul, f32->bf16 back-cast to.dtype, weight-scale mul for the hidden/q/k norm shapes (2263+1116+1116 chains per run); (b) RoPE chains - q/k mul by cos, neg, cat, mul by sin, final add (1116 chains each); (c) the SiLU*up mul. Together they account for 54.6 ms of device time over 33,604 tiny invocations (~1-2 us each, launch-bound). A joint candidate is required because the edits need one another: cooperating replacements thread stub state from the first op of each chain to a single fused materializer (one kernel per chain instead of 4-5), eliminating ~23,530 of 66,064 kernel launches per run (~36%) plus their cudaLaunch/dispatch costs, while every folded op is elementwise with aten's fp32 opmath and bf16 rounding points replicated exactly (round after each aten-visible intermediate, same libdevice rsqrtf/expf), so outputs stay byte-identical - no reduction order anywhere changes.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing the 26 selected decode elementwise sites with stub-threaded, byte-identical fused kernels (one materializer per norm tail, per RoPE chain, and for SiLU*up) cuts ~23.5k kernel launches and ~33.6k full aten dispatches per run. Expected effect: device time on these chains falls from 54.6 ms to ~11-15 ms and the per-step launch/dispatch share of the ~170 ms wall gap falls proportionally, giving a projected end-to-end reduction of roughly 40-90 ms on ~731 ms, i.e. generated_tokens_per_second from ~350 to ~372-405 tok/s (+6-15%), above the MAD-derived paired noise bounds (5.3-8.7 tok/s). Quality/feasibility risks and controls: (1) bit-exactness of fused elementwise math is verified per site class by a first-invocation bitwise comparison against the parent op chain, with permanent per-site fallback to the parent aten op on any mismatch (deterministic inputs make a passing check stable); (2) stub threading through shared mul/add families is disambiguated by shape, dtype direction and stub identity, with passthrough for unrelated sites (residual adds, entry casts, pow/mean/eps-add, GEMMs, sdpa, workspace copies all keep executing the parent path); (3) the accepted bundle stays effective coexistence, not fallback-only: its module call and its GEMM/mean/sdpa kernels continue every step, and all 26 selected calls remain invoked through the replacements. If the combination is correct but does not clear the noise bounds, it is still a valid rejected composition experiment; fallback-only new code is not.

proposal.rationale: Composition, not replacement: the accepted eager flat-decode bundle trial-0b17ae710c-param-a2600a0f (decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM.forward, call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9) stays installed and keeps executing every decode step with its GEMM/mean/sdpa kernels contributing to the current-input result; the 62 observed parent-decoder invocations with zero reference calls in the screen are exactly this behavior. This second candidate returns replacements for the 26 selected decode elementwise sites that all have site_parent 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, so functional dispatch composes inside the region implementation. Repairs made in this attempt, each driven by recorded evidence: (1) the sibling composition trial-fa955139a3 collapsed to fallback-only through a lazy CUDA-graph verification gate and its resample crashed in a silu bits-equal self-test - no stream capture is used anywhere here; (2) the leased GPU probe of the prior draft (inputs/draft-cuda-probe.json) caught a real CompilationError (tl.arange with a non-constexpr bound) in the first RoPE kernel and a verify-chain key error that silently dropped the RoPE add site to the parent - both fixed; (3) the same probe measured the native parent final-add output as contiguous (4096,128,128,1)/(1024,128,128,1) while qc keeps the transposed stride - the fused final tensor is now allocated with the measured native contiguous stride and qc/neg/cat keep their exact aten strides via as_strided allocations; (4) the full-project screen (inputs/draft-project-screen.json) passed both continuous checks with exact greedy tokens but showed max_abs_error 0.125 with the draft's transcendental-in-kernel paths (in-kernel rsqrt from mean+eps, fused silu exp/div) - those two mechanisms are removed entirely, so no byte-identical claim is made or needed for them. What remains executes only IEEE single-precision mul/add/neg with explicit round-to-nearest-even BF16 materialization exactly where the parent aten chain materializes BF16 tensors: (a) each RMSNorm tail's x32*rstd mul site launches one Triton kernel writing both the fp32 product and its BF16 back-cast, the to.dtype site returns that tensor (3 kernels -> 2 per chain, 4495 chains per run); (b) each RoPE chain's q*cos site launches one kernel writing qc=rnd(q*cos), neg(q2) and cat(neg(q2),q1), and the rot*sin site launches a second kernel writing rs=rnd(rot*sin) and final=rnd(qc+rs) (5 kernels -> 2 per chain, 2232 chains per run); the neg/cat/add sites return those genuine-content tensors. The rsqrt, entry-cast, weight-scale-mul and SiLU sites delegate to the real parent operator serving the real computation - no dummy native calls fill coverage. Every replacement guards the full observed shape/stride/dtype signature and falls back per-call; chain linking uses object identity plus base-pointer ties; each fused class is compared chain-by-chain against the live parent op chain with torch.equal over a window covering every chain of one complete run (normQ/K 1200, normH 2300, ropeQ/K 1200 chains, all consumed within the two warmup invocations on the deterministic frozen workload), latching permanently to the parent on any mismatch. That window is a per-workload tripwire, not a general proof; the authoritative gate stays the framework's full quality validation. Projected effect is a hypothesis, not measured attribution: roughly 11.2k fewer kernel launches and a similar order of aten dispatches removed from the overhead-bound decode (~170 ms wall gap over ~2000 launches per step in current discovery), which must clear the paired MAD noise bounds (5.3-8.7 tok/s) in the framework's AB/BA measurement; a correct active combination that fails to clear them is a valid rejected experiment.
proposal.setup_work: No CUDA work at build time: build only validates references and installs closures. On the first decode invocations (warmup, outside timed measure runs): Triton JIT compiles three kernels (_k_norm two BLOCK variants, _k_rope1, _k_rope2), and the verification window runs each fused class chain-by-chain alongside the parent chain with torch.equal, briefly duplicating one chain's intermediates (<1 MB transient per chain, reused via the caching allocator) and synchronizing once per verified chain. Steady-state allocations mirror the parent shapes exactly (qc as an as_strided tensor with the transposed aten stride, neg/cat/rs/final contiguous, fp32 x32 product tensors), so peak_allocated impact is neutral-to-slightly-lower from fewer concurrent intermediates; retained state is limited to compiled Triton kernels and small per-class chain records. No CUDA graphs, no stream capture, no model-parameter transforms, no fixture-dependent caching; the workload executes fully on current inputs every invocation.
quality_risks: Fused-class exactness: the remaining fused kernels are value-independent IEEE mul/add/neg with explicit intermediate BF16 rounding, but each class is still guarded by a per-chain torch.equal window spanning one complete run's chains; any mismatch (including any Triton codegen surprise) permanently reverts that class to the parent path, which can silently erase the performance effect while preserving outputs.

Stride metadata: qc/neg/cat outputs replicate the observed aten strides exactly and rs/final use the native contiguous strides measured by the leased GPU probe; if the worker produced different metadata the signature guards would fall back per-call to the parent (correct values, no fusion).

The verification window is a per-workload tripwire, not a general proof of equivalence; the framework's full continuous quality checks remain the authoritative gate, and the earlier draft showed that adding transcendental kernels can pass thresholds with small nonzero error (max_abs_error 0.125) - which is why those mechanisms were removed rather than kept.

Coexistence: the accepted bundle's module call must keep executing with its own kernels every decode step (it does - it is untouched and its aten chains are what these replacements intercept); if the framework ever routed a site away from these replacements the pristine parent op runs, yielding parent-exact values.

Performance risk: the projected ~11.2k fewer launches/dispatches per run is an unmeasured hypothesis; the paired gain may fall within the MAD-derived noise bounds (5.3-8.7 tok/s), in which case this is a valid rejected composition experiment rather than an accepted one.

Runtime failure handling: any exception inside a replacement routes that call to the parent operator and disables the affected class (distinct labels for setup/unsupported-signature/runtime fallback); all stub returns carry genuine parent-equivalent bytes, so consumers never observe placeholder values.
